answer: Onboard each identity through a slow, sequential proof-of-work that cannot be parallelized, bound to one hardware attestation per device. A fresh identity starts hollow: it may observe but cannot earn until its delay task completes and peers verify its attestation. An orchard of fake agents would need one device and hours of wall-clock time per identity, so bulk creation costs real hardware and real time. Like karst terrain, identities that look solid on the surface collapse when probed, because a copied attestation or a skipped delay is detectable and the identity is burned.
